## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Normalize keys on write so callers can retrieve entries stored with mixed-case keys.

## Changes

The pull request adds `Cache.set` and increases the default TTL from 60 to 300 seconds. It adds tests for lookup, the default TTL constant, and expiration with a custom TTL.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Normalize keys in Cache.set — After `set("Alpha", 1)`, `get("Alpha")` returns `None`. The setter stores `"Alpha"`, while the getter looks up `"alpha"`. — Callers miss cached values, and those entries bypass the getter’s expiration cleanup. — Fix: Lowercase the key before storing it and extend `test_set_then_get_round_trip` with a mixed-case write.

## Suggestions

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Expire entries at their deadline — An entry written at clock time `1000.0` with a one-second TTL is still returned at `1001.0`. The setter records that deadline, and `get` removes the entry only when the clock exceeds it. — A lookup at the exact expiration time can receive a value whose TTL has elapsed. — Fix: Use `expires <= time.monotonic()` at `app/cache.py:21` and extend `test_entries_expire`.
- app/cache.py:8 — tests — Test the default TTL through cache lookups — For a default cache whose setter mistakenly retains the old 60-second lifetime, `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` still passes because it checks only the class constant. The expiration test supplies an explicit TTL. — The tests can miss a regression that shortens the lifetime of entries written with the default settings. — Fix: Update `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` to exercise expiration through `set` and `get`.
